extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers; journal editors; research institutions training reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical and practical guidance for researchers acting as peer reviewers for scholarly journals, covering pre-review decisions, conduct during review, report preparation, and post-review responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept only reviews within your subject expertise and time availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Only agree to review manuscripts for which you have the subject expertise required to carry out a proper assessment and which you can assess in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot assess all aspects, declare which parts you can assess. Only agree if fairly confident you can return a review within the proposed or mutually agreed time-frame, and inform the journal promptly if you require an extension. Do not agree just to see the manuscript without intending to submit a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect confidentiality of manuscripts and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the confidentiality of peer review and not reveal any details of a manuscript or its review, during or after the peer-review process, beyond those that are released by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue to keep details of the manuscript and its review confidential after submission. Do not contact the authors directly without the permission of the journal. Refrain from looking at the manuscript while awaiting instructions if the journal may rescind the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misuse information from peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Not use information obtained during the peer-review process for their own or any other person’s or organization’s advantage, or to disadvantage or discredit others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes avoiding using privileged information to advance your research, to pre-empt publication, or to harm authors' reputations. Do not attempt to investigate suspected misconduct personally; report concerns to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare all potential conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare all potential conflicting interests, seeking advice from the journal if they are unsure whether something constitutes a relevant interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts can be personal, financial, intellectual, professional, political or religious. If unsure, ask the journal. Notify the journal immediately if you discover a conflict after agreeing to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bias based on authors' characteristics or commercial considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Not allow their reviews to be influenced by the origins of a manuscript, by the nationality, religious or political beliefs, gender or other characteristics of the authors, or by commercial considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure evaluations are based solely on the merits of the work and not on external attributes or commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be objective and constructive; avoid hostile or defamatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Be objective and constructive in their reviews, refraining from being hostile or inflammatory and from making libellous or derogatory personal comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase criticisms to help authors improve; avoid ad hominem attacks, hostility, or language that could be defamatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept reciprocal duty to review fairly and timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that peer review is largely a reciprocal endeavour and undertake to carry out their fair share of reviewing and in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to review requests and attempt to contribute to the community's reviewing needs rather than only consuming review opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate personal and professional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide journals with personal and professional information that is accurate and a true representation of their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewer databases and communications reflect true expertise and affiliations so editors can make appropriate reviewer selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize impersonation as serious misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that impersonation of another individual during the review process is considered serious misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impersonate others; report suspected impersonation to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to review invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond in a reasonable time-frame, especially if they cannot do the review, and without intentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly accept or decline so the editor can find alternative reviewers if necessary. Provide an accurate estimate of time needed if you can do the review but need longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare partial expertise when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare if they do not have the subject expertise required to carry out the review or if they are able to assess only part of the manuscript, outlining clearly the areas for which they have the relevant expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If able to assess only certain sections (e.g., methods but not background), state that clearly to the editor so they can decide how to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare potentially conflicting or competing interests with examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any potentially conflicting or competing interests (which may, for example, be personal, financial, intellectual, professional, political or religious), seeking advice from the journal if unsure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include working at the same institution as an author, being a recent mentor/mentee or close collaborator (e.g., within past 3 years), joint grant holders, or close personal relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow or seek guidance on journal conflict policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow journals’ policies on situations they consider to represent a conflict to reviewing. If no guidance is provided, inform the journal of relevant relationships (same institution, recent mentors/mentees/collaborators/joint grant holders, close personal relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, disclose. Journals may have different thresholds and prefer to make the decision on suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-review manuscripts previously reviewed elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Review afresh any manuscript they have previously reviewed for another journal as it may have changed between the two submissions and the journals’ criteria for evaluation and acceptance may be different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume previous evaluation applies; examine the current version and current journal's criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternative reviewers based on suitability alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure suggestions for alternative reviewers are based on suitability and not influenced by personal considerations or made with the intention of the manuscript receiving a specific outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not recommend reviewers because they will provide a favorable or unfavorable review; choose based on expertise and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline when unable to provide a fair and unbiased review
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline to review if they feel unable to provide a fair and unbiased review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes emotional or ideological inability to be impartial, or when a conflict can't be managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline when involved with the manuscript work or reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline to review if they have been involved with any of the work in the manuscript or its reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reviewing work where you contributed to the research, analysis, or writing to maintain impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline when manuscript is very similar to reviewer’s own work in preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline to review if asked to review a manuscript that is very similar to one they have in preparation or under consideration at another journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarity could create conflicts of interest or competitive harm; disclose and decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline if peer-review model conflicts with reviewer’s ability to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline to review if they have issues with the peer-review model used by a journal (e.g. open review releasing reviewers’ names) that would affect their review or invalidate it because of inability to comply with the journal’s review policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If open review would compromise anonymity or present unacceptable risks, inform the editor and decline if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify journal immediately of newly discovered conflicts or issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the journal immediately and seek advice if they discover either a conflicting interest that wasn’t apparent when they agreed to the review or anything that might prevent them providing a fair and unbiased review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt disclosure allows the editor to reassign or manage the review appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from using manuscripts before journal instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from looking at the manuscript and associated material while awaiting instructions from a journal on issues that might cause the request to review to be rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an editor asks you not to proceed until they advise, comply to avoid breeches of confidentiality or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read manuscript and ancillary materials thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the manuscript, ancillary material (e.g. reviewer instructions, required ethics and policy statements, supplemental data files) and journal instructions thoroughly, getting back to the journal if anything is not clear and requesting any missing or incomplete items needed to carry out a full review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you have all necessary files and understand journal-specific criteria before concluding your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify promptly if lack expertise during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the journal as soon as possible if they find they do not have the expertise to assess all aspects of the manuscript; they shouldn’t wait until submitting their review as this will unduly delay the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early notification helps editors secure other reviewers and prevents wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permission before involving others and credit helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: Not involve anyone else in the review of a manuscript, including junior researchers they are mentoring, without first obtaining permission from the journal; the names of any individuals who have helped them with the review should be included with the returned review so they are associated with the manuscript in the journal’s records and can also receive due credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you ask a colleague or trainee to assist, disclose their contribution and obtain editorial approval to protect confidentiality and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep manuscript and review details confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep all manuscript and review details confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscripts, data, or review contents with others unless explicitly permitted by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate promptly about delays and give realistic timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the journal if circumstances arise that will prevent them from submitting a timely review, providing an accurate estimate of the time they will need to do a review if still asked to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid intentionally prolonging the process or requesting unnecessary additional information to delay decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose suspected author identity in double-blind only if it raises conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of double-blind review, if they suspect the identity of the author(s) notify the journal if this knowledge raises any potential conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not act on suspicions except to inform the editor; let the editor manage any changes to the review assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report ethical concerns, irregularities, or plagiarism to the journal confidentially
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify the journal immediately if they come across any irregularities, have concerns about ethical aspects of the work, are aware of substantial similarity between the manuscript and a concurrent submission to another journal or a published article, or suspect that misconduct may have occurred during either the research or the writing and submission of the manuscript; reviewers should keep their concerns confidential and not personally investigate further unless the journal asks for further information or advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the journal with details and any evidence you have; do not contact authors or conduct independent inquiries that could compromise investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intentionally prolonging the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Not intentionally prolong the review process, either by delaying the submission of their review or by requesting unnecessary additional information from the journal or author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be efficient and only request information essential to a fair assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base review on merits; avoid influence from conflicts or intellectual biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure their review is based on the merits of the work and not influenced, either positively or negatively, by any personal, financial, or other conflicting considerations or by intellectual biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and mitigate your own biases; disclose influences that cannot be managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide subject-knowledge, good judgement, and honest assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Bear in mind that the editor is looking to them for subject knowledge, good judgement, and an honest and fair assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the work and the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure reviews to highlight strengths and weaknesses and to support the editor's decision-making with clear reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: State scope of requested review at the start of the report
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear at the start of their review if they have been asked to address only specific parts or aspects of a manuscript and indicate which these are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps editors and authors understand what was evaluated and what remains unassessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal instructions on feedback format and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow journals’ instructions on the specific feedback that is required of them and, unless there are good reasons not to, the way this should be organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If journals request structured headings or separate comments for editors and authors, follow those templates for clarity and editorial workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback to help authors improve
rubrics_metrics.description: Be objective and constructive in their reviews and provide feedback that will help the authors to improve their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable suggestions, identify required vs optional changes, and prioritize major issues over minor stylistic preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid derogatory personal comments or unfounded accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Not make derogatory personal comments or unfounded accusations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have concerns about integrity, report them to the editor rather than making accusations in the public review comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific in criticisms and provide evidence/references
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific in their criticisms, and provide evidence with appropriate references to substantiate general statements such as, 'this work has been done before', to help editors in their evaluation and decision and in fairness to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior work or evidence supporting claims of prior art, methodological flaws, or factual errors so authors and editors can verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rewriting authors' papers to own style; suggest clarity improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember it is the authors’ paper and not attempt to rewrite it to their own preferred style if it is basically sound and clear; suggestions for changes that improve clarity are, however, important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on necessary improvements to clarity, logic, and validity rather than imposing stylistic preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive about language issues for non-native speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the sensitivities surrounding language issues that are due to the authors writing in a language that is not their own, and phrase the feedback appropriately and with due respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive, respectful language-editing suggestions rather than derisive comments about grammar or phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate essential vs optional additional investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear which suggested additional investigations are essential to support claims made in the manuscript under consideration and which will just strengthen or extend the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label recommendations as 'required' vs 'suggested' so editors and authors understand the impact on acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not imply that another person prepared the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Not prepare their report in such a way or include comments that suggest the review has been done by another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If others assisted, disclose their names per journal policy rather than disguising their contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preparing reports that reflect badly or unfairly on others
rubrics_metrics.description: Not prepare their report in a way that reflects badly or unfairly on another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments professional and focused on the manuscript rather than attacking third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unfair negative comments about competitors’ work
rubrics_metrics.description: Not make unfair negative comments or include unjustified criticisms of any competitors’ work that is mentioned in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should be evidence-based and not motivated by rivalry; provide references if questioning prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency between comments to editor and authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure their comments and recommendations for the editor are consistent with their report for the authors; most feedback should be put in the report for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve confidential, essential concerns for the editor but avoid using that space for denigration or false accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use confidential comments for denigration or false accusation
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the editor should not be a place for denigration or false accusation, done in the knowledge that the authors will not see these comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential notes should be factual, corroborated, and relevant to editorial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid citation self-interest; suggest citations only for valid reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Not suggest that authors include citations to the reviewer’s (or their associates’) work merely to increase the reviewer’s (or their associates’) citation count or to enhance visibility; suggestions must be based on valid academic or technological reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending your own work, declare the relationship and justify why it is necessary or helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to sign the review according to journal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the journal allows them to sign their reviews and, if it does, decide as they feel comfortable doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing is optional when permitted; weigh benefits and risks (e.g., courteous accountability vs potential reprisals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors providing a review must be transparent about it
rubrics_metrics.description: If they are the editor handling a manuscript and decide themselves to provide a review of that manuscript, do this transparently and not under the guise of an anonymous review if the journal operates blind review; providing a review for a manuscript being handled by another editor at the journal can be treated as any other review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid secrecy when editors review manuscripts they handle to prevent conflicts and ensure trust in editorial processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to post-review journal queries promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly if contacted by a journal about matters related to their review of a manuscript and provide the information required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may ask clarifications after initial submission; timely follow-up aids decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform journal of post-submission developments that affect review
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the journal if anything relevant comes to light after they have submitted their review that might affect their original feedback and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discover new conflicts, errors, or information that would change your appraisal, inform the editor so they can reassess decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read other reviewers’ reports when provided to learn and understand decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the reviews from the other reviewers, if these are provided by the journal, to improve their own understanding of the topic or the decision reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a development opportunity and to calibrate future reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try to review revisions or resubmissions when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to accommodate requests from journals to review revisions or resubmissions of manuscripts they have reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, continue involvement to assess whether authors addressed prior concerns; disclose if unable to do so.
